interludes.speaker: ops
interludes.text: Lunar night falls in {nightIn} days: 14 days with zero sunlight. Ration heating now to stockpile power?

interludes.speaker: eng
interludes.text: A crater rim near the pole gets sunlight almost all month. Moving the solar farm there takes 4 days.
interludes.fact: Some lunar south pole peaks are sunlit most of the time. It's a big reason Artemis targets the pole.

interludes.speaker: sci
interludes.text: A crater that never sees sunlight holds ancient ice, but it's below −200°C down there. Go on a 2-day expedition?
interludes.fact: Some polar craters haven't seen sunlight in billions of years.

interludes.speaker: sci
interludes.text: A far-side expedition could reveal amazing geology. That's 3 days with no contact with Earth.
interludes.fact: The far side never faces Earth, so you need a relay satellite to call home.

interludes.speaker: arch
interludes.text: Sunlit surfaces hit +120°C and shadows drop to −170°C. Add thermal blankets? 2 days of work.
interludes.fact: With no air to hold heat, the Moon swings from scorching to freezing.

interludes.speaker: med
interludes.text: Moondust is sharp like glass and it's getting into everyone's lungs. Install a dust airlock?
interludes.fact: Apollo astronauts said moondust smelled like spent gunpowder.

interludes.speaker: hq
interludes.text: An Artemis crew wants to visit for 3 days. Great for spirits, but more mouths to feed.
interludes.fact: NASA's Artemis program aims for a long-term human presence on the Moon.

interludes.speaker: arch
interludes.text: Rocket landings sandblast the base with dust. Bake a landing pad from regolith? That's 3 days.
interludes.fact: Landing engines spray lunar dust at high speed. Hard pads protect nearby gear.

interludes.speaker: ops
interludes.text: Seismometers picked up a moonquake. Inspect every structure? It takes 2 days.
interludes.fact: Apollo seismometers recorded moonquakes. Some shallow ones lasted about 10 minutes.

interludes.speaker: sci
interludes.text: Moon rock is about 40% oxygen by mass! Our reactor can bake it out if we feed it power.
interludes.fact: Heating lunar soil to release oxygen is a key ISRU technology.

interludes.speaker: com
interludes.text: Earth sits low on the horizon here and hills block it. Build a taller mast? 2 days.
interludes.fact: Radio needs a clear line of sight. Near the poles, Earth hugs the horizon.
